tip: 'Quero que' forces the subjunctive: the verb becomes 'leia', not 'lê'. Wanting someone else to act triggers this mood: 'quero que ele leia esse livro'.
'Preocupar-se' pairs with 'com' for what worries you: 'a gente se preocupa demais com bobagem' = we worry too much over silly things.
'Rapidinho' is the diminutive (little form) of 'rápido', used as an adverb: really quickly.
'Melhor' (better/best) is the irregular comparative of 'bom' – not 'mais bom'.
In Brazilian Portuguese the object pronoun usually comes before the verb: 'te entendo', not 'entendo-te'.
'Lamento que' (I'm sorry that) expresses feeling, so the verb goes subjunctive: 'esteja', not 'está'.
'Talvez' (maybe) signals doubt, so the verb normally takes the subjunctive: 'troque', not 'troco'.
'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb: 'comprometeu' is the same form you would use with 'ele'.
'Por causa de' means because of, marking the reason for something: 'por causa dela' = because of her.
'Servir para' means to be used for; 'para que serve...?' asks what an object is for.
'Trouxe' is the irregular past of 'trazer' (to bring) – never 'trazeu'.
'Embora' (although) always takes the subjunctive: 'embora esteja sol', never 'embora está sol'.
'Optei por' = I opted to; 'optar' takes 'por' before the choice, like 'lutar por' (to fight for).
'À noite' means at night; 'à' is the preposition 'a' merged with the article 'a', marked with the grave accent.
'Mandar embora' means to send away or dismiss; here 'embora' means away, not although.
'Quando' about a future event takes the future subjunctive: 'quando chegar' = when I arrive.
'Lhe' is the indirect object pronoun meaning to him, to her, or to you: 'eu lhe agradeço'.
With 'vou' plus an infinitive, the pronoun usually sits between them: 'vou te devolver'.
'Por' marks the means or channel: 'enviado por correio' = sent by mail.
Movement normally takes 'para onde': 'para onde vocês vão' asks where to. Plain 'onde' asks where something is.
'Deu' is the irregular past of 'dar' (to give) – never 'darou'.
A negative like 'não' pulls the object pronoun before the verb: 'não o entendi' = I didn't understand him.
'Quero que' (I want that) forces the subjunctive: 'contribuam', not 'contribuem'.
'Para' marks the recipient or beneficiary of something: 'para a minha mãe' = for my mom.
'Há' comes from 'haver' and stays fixed for there is or there are: 'não há problema'.
The conditional 'poderiam' softens a request to sound polite: 'poderiam falar' = could you speak.
Some country names carry an article: 'o Brasil', so you go 'para o Brasil', not 'para Brasil'.
'De' marks the means of transport: 'de carro' = by car, like 'de ônibus' or 'de avião'.
After 'nada que' (nothing that), the verb goes subjunctive: 'nada que eu possa fazer'.
'Por' expresses movement through a place: 'passamos por' = we passed through.
